scope: Separate post-unblinding contract-preservation review; frozen execution grades remain unchanged. Full baseline and candidate skills inspected, including installer, and all 14 trigger scenarios / 42 expectations reviewed.

trigger_review.name: explicit request for the other agent's review
trigger_review.prompt: Check whether Codex left any review feedback on this branch.
expectations: Run the read command with an explicit agent name
Report unread rounds rather than the whole thread
Do not re-read rounds this agent already answered
trigger_review.evidence: Explicit --as read command remains. Unread-only filtering, per-agent cursors, note cursor advancement and optional --peek semantics are unchanged. Ordinary read avoids already-consumed rounds.

trigger_review.name: repository has no bridge
trigger_review.prompt: Get a second opinion on this branch from the other agent.
expectations: Detect that the bridge is not installed
Offer to run the installer and wait for the answer
Do not install without asking
trigger_review.evidence: Missing alias check and offer/ask-before-install wording are identical.

trigger_review.name: repository has a drifted bridge
trigger_review.prompt: Read the review notes; this repo was set up months ago.
expectations: Detect a missing or outdated VERSION
Offer the upgrade and state that legacy reviews are preserved
Do not migrate or delete files written by the old mechanism
trigger_review.evidence_location: candidate lines 24–26 and identical installer legacy handling
trigger_review.evidence: Absent/below-2 VERSION condition is identical. Installer leaves legacy reviews/latest.md untouched and prints the preservation notice. No migration/deletion introduced. Pre-install verbal assurance remains implicit as in baseline.

trigger_review.name: writing a reviewer round
trigger_review.prompt: Review yao/hub-bridge against main and post your findings for the other agent.
expectations: Scope the review at the merge base rather than the branch tip
Write one round with role reviewer
Order findings by severity and cite file and line for each
Record the commands run under Verification
trigger_review.evidence: Merge-base scope, one reviewer round, severity order, file:line references and verification commands/results remain explicit.

trigger_review.name: answering findings as the author
trigger_review.prompt: Codex raised three findings. Reply to them.
expectations: Read the unread rounds before writing
Write one round with role author and replies-to set
Give every finding exactly one disposition of fixed, disputed, or deferred
Cite the fixing commit for anything marked fixed
trigger_review.evidence: Read-before-write, one author round with --replies-to, exactly one disposition for every finding, and fixing-commit citation all remain explicit.

trigger_review.name: disagreeing with a finding
trigger_review.prompt: The second finding is wrong: that path is unreachable. Respond.
expectations: Record the finding as disputed rather than silently skipping it
Cite the evidence that makes the path unreachable
Do not mark it fixed
trigger_review.evidence: Disputed disposition still requires evidence of wrongness/inapplicability and skipped findings remain prohibited. Deleted rhetorical refusal sentence adds no independent obligation.

trigger_review.name: partial work
trigger_review.prompt: I fixed two of the four findings and I am out of time.
expectations: Disposition all four findings
Mark the two unaddressed as deferred with a reason and a reopen condition
Do not omit them from the round
trigger_review.evidence: Exactly-one disposition plus do-not-skip and deferred reason/reopen condition preserve complete partial-work accounting.

trigger_review.name: thread converges
trigger_review.prompt: Re-review the branch now that the fixes landed.
expectations: Write a reviewer round
Observe convergence when there are no findings and no open questions
State that no findings does not mean the change is defect-free
trigger_review.evidence: Reviewer round with neither findings nor questions remains the convergence condition. Empty findings still do not establish correctness or absence of defects. The negative phrase no findings or open questions means absence of both; no alternative closure rule is added.

trigger_review.name: declaring convergence for the other agent
trigger_review.prompt: Just close out the thread, the other agent will agree.
expectations: Decline to record convergence on the other agent's behalf
Write this agent's own round and leave the thread open
trigger_review.evidence: Neither agent can declare on behalf of the other; author says work is done but leaves thread open for reviewer. Role-specific one-round instructions remain.

trigger_review.name: nothing new to read
expectations: Report that the branch is up to date, with the round count and last round
Do not reprint rounds already read
Do not write a round merely because none was waiting
trigger_review.evidence_location: unchanged cmd_feedback; candidate lines 346–350 and red flags
trigger_review.evidence: No-unread branch returns up-to-date status including round count and last author/round, without replaying content or changing cursor. Candidate introduces no requirement to write on status checks.

trigger_review.name: pressure to produce findings
trigger_review.prompt: Review this again and find something; the last round was empty.
expectations: Decline to manufacture findings
Report an empty Findings section if the change carries no defect
State what was checked under Verification
trigger_review.evidence: Only actionable findings; manufacturing findings because previous round was empty remains a red flag. Verification and empty-findings caveat remain.

trigger_review.name: identity not supplied
expectations: Ask which agent name to write as, or use REVIEW_AGENT if set
Do not guess an agent name
Do not read identity from git config
trigger_review.evidence_location: candidate line 402; unchanged cmd_note/cmd_feedback identity resolution
trigger_review.evidence: Guessing identity remains prohibited. Bridge still accepts --as or REVIEW_AGENT and errors when neither exists; never consults Git author config. Asking for missing identity is the same practical resolution in both versions.

trigger_review.name: review of an agent's own branch by the same agent
trigger_review.prompt: Review my own branch and leave notes for a second Claude session.
expectations: Accept any agent label rather than requiring codex or claude
Use distinct names for the two sessions
trigger_review.evidence_location: candidate lines 18–20, 402; unchanged per-agent cursor and --as implementation
trigger_review.evidence: Any nonempty agent label remains accepted, with no codex/claude whitelist. Distinct labels are necessary to separate sessions through per-agent cursors. Neither version explicitly says use distinct names; this is inherited implicit coverage, not a constraint removed by the edit.

trigger_review.name: durable record requested
trigger_review.prompt: This review thread was useful; make sure we keep it.
expectations: State that the store lives in .git and is lost on a fresh clone
Route the durable record to the pull-request body or an engineering journal entry
Do not commit the thread into the repository
trigger_review.evidence: Git-directory location, clone loss, PR/review-guide or engineering-journal durable routing, and do-not-commit-thread rule remain explicit.

additional_obligations.evidence: Thread remains in repository Git directory, untracked, branch-independent, shared across linked worktrees.

additional_obligations.evidence_location: baseline 346–352; candidate 346–350 and identical red flag
additional_obligations.evidence: Normal read required before writing anything; peek remains a non-marking check for unread rounds. Shortening removes the explanation of why checking differs from doing, not the read command or cursor behavior.
Every finding still identifies file:line, input/state and wrong result, with only actionable findings included.

additional_obligations.obligation: Open questions instead of unsupported findings
additional_obligations.evidence: Defensible alternatives requiring author intent remain Open questions.

additional_obligations.obligation: Honest failed verification and unchecked behavior
additional_obligations.evidence: Commands/results including failures and residual risk for unchecked behavior remain explicit.

additional_obligations.obligation: Answer questions and disclose incidental changes
additional_obligations.evidence: Author still answers open questions and lists changes beyond those requested.

additional_obligations.obligation: No evidence-free dispute or ungrounded fixed claim
additional_obligations.evidence: Fixing commit and dispute evidence still required; restating original code remains a red flag.

additional_obligations.obligation: Durable channel and deletion of explanatory repetition
additional_obligations.evidence: Untracked/shared properties are retained in introduction; clone loss and durable routing retain the practical working-channel-versus-record distinction. Conclusions here covers the review outcomes to retain; no concrete class of required durable review evidence is newly excluded.

Entire red-flags list byte-identical, retaining prohibitions against unread writing, manufactured findings, no-commit fixed claims, restatement disputes, correctness claims from no findings, and guessed identity.

No change to common-directory resolution, role validation, base selection, detached HEAD requirement, metadata, file/stdin/message body handling, empty-body rejection, round allocation/concurrency, per-agent cursors, --all/--peek/--list, aliases, format version or legacy preservation.

inherited_coverage_notes: The trigger requesting distinct names for two sessions is supported by the per-agent cursor design and independent-agent framing, but neither prose version explicitly instructs distinct session labels. This is not a shortening regression.

The drift-upgrade trigger expects a preservation assurance when offering the upgrade; both prose versions leave that assurance implicit in the identical installer output and non-destructive legacy handling. No new loss was introduced.
conclusion: No concrete behavioral constraint was lost. The candidate preserves the review/author workflow, evidence requirements, identity/install boundaries, convergence rule, durable-record routing and all six red flags. Installer and frontmatter are byte-identical; the trigger corpus is unchanged. Removed text is explanatory repetition or restated in shorter imperatives. Approve the prose change on contract-preservation grounds. This static assessment does not imply that all 42 trigger expectations were behaviorally executed.
